key_insight: p-ResNet-50 augments a ResNet-50 backbone with a prototype layer so the model not only detects defects in X‑ray CT of SiC/SiC composites but also points to prototypical image regions that justify each decision, enabling traceable, visual explanations.
problem_solved: Automates defect detection in XCT scans while addressing the lack of transparency and traceability in expert accept/reject decisions by providing interpretable, evidence-based outputs instead of black‑box predictions.
method: Backbone: ResNet-50 convolutional encoder adapted to XCT slice inputs for defect candidate extraction.
Prototype layer: learnable prototypical image patches that the model compares to activation maps to localize and justify detections.
Training & evaluation: supervised learning on labeled XCT data with joint loss terms for classification accuracy and prototype similarity to ensure meaningful visual explanations.
impact: Provides a practical path to deploy high‑performance CV models in regulated industrial inspection workflows by coupling automated defect detection with human‑readable, traceable evidence — improving acceptance by inspectors and easing certification.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: ResNet-50 backbone feeding a prototype layer with arrows showing prototype matching and final prediction.
Prototype gallery: grid of learned prototypical patches annotated with the defects they represent (e.g., voids, cracks, delaminations).
Before/after XCT slice examples: original scan, model heatmap/localization, and overlay of the matched prototype for the decision.
Performance + interpretability chart: side‑by‑side bar/ROC plots for detection metrics and a simple score for explanation fidelity/consistency.
paper_title: Interpretable Computer Vision for Defect Detection in X-ray Tomography of Aerospace SiC/SiC Composites
paper_authors: Antonio Peña Corredor, Julien Lesseur, Romain Nunez, Paul Rivalland, Thomas Philippe
